issues.body: The test constructs `v1` without a thread-local override, but `encode_emit` intentionally falls back to `SPARQ_EMIT_FORMAT`. If the test process is launched with that variable set to `v2`, the asserted default-V1 invariant fails even though production behavior is correct. This makes the test sensitive to ambient configuration and means it does not strictly test the claimed no-override state.
issues.fix_hint: Construct the V1 store with `with_emit_format(EmitFormat::V1, || TripleStore::from_triples_compressed(...))`, while keeping the V2 construction explicitly overridden as it is now.
issues.title: Default-V1 assertion depends on ambient SPARQ_EMIT_FORMAT

verdict.summary: The change correctly routes the in-memory compressed-store construction through the existing emit-format policy while preserving the feature-off path as the original V1 encoder. The feature relationships are coherent (`spqcprm2` implies `mmap`), V2 permutations retain the format needed by the decoder, and the public-surface documentation is updated. The added test exercises the real store construction and scan paths across both formats and compares them with the raw store. One minor test-isolation issue remains: its purported default-V1 construction can inherit a process environment override.
